ÃƒÂ¢Ã¢â€šÂ¬Ã‚Â¢ Bug found+fixed in the search backend: when the AI extracts listings from the raw search results, the de-duplication step trusted whatever link the AI attached to each listing without checking it was one of the links we actually gave it. â€¢ Verified live on brendanlok.github.io/partfinder: real 8-listing VW Golf search, applied a 15.000 â‚¬ min-price filter - the below/above-market badges stayed identical to the unfiltered view (before the fix, filtering would have stripped the badge off two mid-priced cars). No console errors.

• 3pm session: Telegram inbox empty. Board still 5/5 Backlog (all NEEDS LOK'S CALL) - ran a code audit of the frontend (page.tsx / lib helpers), first deep pass on it.
• Bug found+fixed: part prices with cents were parsed 100x too high. The shared price parser stripped every non-digit, so a German part price like "129,95 €" (comma = decimal separator) became 12.995 €. Knock-on: the "Your build" total, "Suggested opening offer" (which then clamped to €0), the seller negotiation draft, the financing estimate and the compare-view build total were all wrong the moment any priced part was added.
• Fix: pulled the parser into src/lib/price.ts with its own self-check - now reads a trailing separator + 2 digits as cents and inner separators as thousands grouping; car prices ("18.500 €") unchanged. Display totals now round to whole euros.
• Verified: all 5 lib self-checks pass, next build clean, new regex confirmed present in the deployed JS bundle, live site loads with no console errors and no horizontal overflow at 375px. No live search spent (parsing fix is unit-covered).

• 5pm session: Telegram inbox empty. Board still 5/5 Backlog (all NEEDS LOK'S CALL) — ran a code audit of the compare view + lib helpers.
• Bug found+fixed: the side-by-side compare screen's "Build total" added up the car price plus every part a lookup returned, but the detail modal's "Your build" for the same car only counts the parts the user actually ticked — so the two screens showed different money figures for one car. Compare now uses the same checked-parts-only math as the modal. Also stopped a no-price / nothing-ticked car showing "0 €" instead of "—".
• Build + TypeScript clean, shipped (6583647). Live page loads with no console errors; full compare-flow re-check would need a real search + condition check + parts lookup — not spent, to protect the shared Tavily/Gemini quota.

text.content:
- 5pm session (2nd item this run): board still 5/5 Backlog (all NEEDS LOK'S CALL). Ran another frontend audit + built the daily idea.
- Bug found+fixed: the duplicate-listing matcher carried its own cut-down price parser (digits only), separate from the corrected one the rest of the app uses. A car price written with cents ("18.900,00 EUR") parsed as 1.890.000, so the "same car cross-posted?" test (prices must agree within 30%) would reject an obvious duplicate, and the "cheapest source first" ordering could invert. Now it shares the one parser in src/lib/price.ts; self-check extended.
- Daily idea (built + shipped): result cards and the detail modal now show annual mileage next to the odometer, e.g. "9.000 km/Jahr". German buyers judge a used car against the ~15.000 km/year TUV average - well below can mean it sat unused or the odometer was wound back, well above means hard use. Pure client-side calc from year + mileage, zero API cost; only shown when both are known.
- Verified live on brendanlok.github.io/partfinder: real VW Golf Mk7 search returned 8 clean listings, correct source tags, no console errors. Injected year+mileage into two listings to exercise the new tag - rendered "9.000 km/Jahr" and "20.000 km/Jahr", both correct, de-DE formatted. next build clean, both lib self-checks pass.
